0.0.n: Points to the story the speaker is about to tell.

0.1.n: Marks これ as the topic of the sentence.

0.2.n: A neutral way to refer to yourself.

0.3.n: Marks 私 as the person who got lost.

0.4.n: A station name; 新宿 is the place name and 駅 means station.

0.5.n: Marks the location where the speaker got lost.

0.6.n: The plain past form of 迷う, describing what happened at that time.

0.7.n: After a verb, 時 refers to the time when that action happened.

0.8.n: Links the whole phrase ending in 時 to 話, identifying what the story concerns.

0.9.n: Refers to an account of the speaker's experience.

0.10.n: A polite sentence ending used after a noun.

1.0.n: Introduces the first point the speaker wants to make.

1.1.n: Combines with に to indicate the first point or step.

1.2.n: Makes 最初に an expression meaning first or at the outset.

1.3.n: 知って + おいて + ほしい expresses wanting the listener to know something in advance.

1.4.n: Turns the preceding description into a noun phrase: the thing the speaker wants you to know.

1.5.n: Marks the thing the speaker wants you to know as the topic.

1.7.n: The speaker explicitly identifies herself or himself before describing a personal trait.

1.8.n: Marks 私 as the topic of the statement about navigation ability.

1.9.n: Combines with 音痴 to describe someone who struggles with navigation.

1.10.n: Literally tone-deaf, 音痴 also describes being bad at something; 方向音痴 means having a poor sense of direction.

1.11.n: Politely completes the description 方向音痴.

2.0.n: Japanese does not require an article such as a before this noun.

2.1.n: Marks 地図 as the thing that exists or is available.

2.2.n: The て-form of ある, which expresses existence; here it means a map is available.

2.3.n: Following a verb's て-form, も shows that the result holds despite that condition.

2.5.n: The polite nonpast form of 迷う describes a recurring tendency here.

3.0.n: Connects the speaker's poor sense of direction to the example that follows.

3.2.n: A brand name, forming the service name Google マップ with the following word.

3.4.n: A word borrowed from English, used here as part of the service name Google Maps.

3.5.n: Marks Google マップ as what the speaker uses.

3.6.n: The て-form of 使う connects to も to express even when using.

3.7.n: Together with 使って, it emphasizes that using maps still does not prevent getting lost.

3.9.n: Describes ところ and needs な before that noun.

3.10.n: Links the describing word 変 to the noun ところ.

3.11.n: Refers to locations; Japanese does not mark this noun as singular or plural.

3.12.n: Marks the destination of the movement expressed by 行く.

3.13.n: Part of 行っちゃったり; ちゃう is casual for てしまう, suggesting an unintended outcome here.

3.14.n: In 行っちゃったりします, たり presents going to strange places as one example of what happens.

3.15.n: The polite form of する completes the たり pattern for giving examples of actions.

0.lit: This, as for, is a story of the time I got lost at Shinjuku Station.
0.tip: 迷った時 means when I got lost, and の connects that whole time phrase to 話.

1.lit: First, at the beginning, the thing I want you to know beforehand: as for me, I am direction-challenged.
1.tip: 知っておいてほしい means the speaker wants the listener to know something in advance.

2.lit: Even if a map exists, I get lost.
2.tip: A verb's て-form plus も means even if or even when.

3.lit: So, even using Google Maps, I do things like end up going to strange places.
3.tip: ちゃう is a casual shortening of てしまう, often suggesting something happened unintentionally or regrettably.
